title: FDA nod for rare neurology drug - Nature Biotechnology
gist: The FDA approved Ionis Pharmaceuticals' Zanvastro (zilganersen), the first disease-modifying drug for Alexander disease, an antisense oligonucleotide that lowers GFAP production in astrocytes. The disease is rare, affecting about one person in 1-3 million.

insights.claim: The FDA approved Ionis Pharmaceuticals' Zanvastro (zilganersen) as the first disease-modifying drug for Alexander disease, a rare, progressive and often fatal neurological condition.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Another antisense approval for Ionis validates RNA-targeted therapy in ultra-rare neurology; watch pricing and uptake in a tiny population.

insights.claim: Zanvastro is an antisense oligonucleotide targeting RNA encoding glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), which is overexpressed in astrocytes because of GFAP gene mutations.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Targeting the mutated gene's RNA output is a template for other gliopathies and toxic gain-of-function diseases.
insights.quote: Zanvastro is an antisense oligonucleotide that targets RNA encoding glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP)

insights.claim: Excess GFAP forms clumps that cause astrocytes to malfunction and disrupt myelination in nerve-cell axons, so reducing GFAP production addresses the underlying cause.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Establishes a mechanistic chain from GFAP overproduction to neurological symptoms that supports the drug's rationale.
insights.quote: If there is too much GFAP, it forms clumps that cause astrocytes to malfunction and disrupt myelination in nerve-cell axons.
